Eight persons, Q, R, S, T, U, V, W and X, sit in a straight row facing north, not necessarily in the same order.

1. Only one person sits between S and V.
2. X sits to the immediate left of R.
3. Only two persons sit between S and Q.
4. S sits second to the left of R.
5. W sits second to the right of T.
6. Q sits to the immediate left of U.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits second to the right of W?

steps: Start with clues 2, 4 and 1: together they fix R, X, S and V.
Clue 3 gives 2 cases — Case 1: Q third to the left of S; Case 2: Q third to the right of S.
Clue 5 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 5 and 6 then place T, W and U.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): T, V, W, S, X, R, Q, U.
Second to the right of W: S → X — answer **X**.
solution.shortcut: Take left/right from the person’s own facing, then count seats along the row.
solution.trap: T is second to the left — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

Clue 5 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 5 and 6 then place T, W and U.

The two end seats hold T and U — **T and U**.
